followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified generation/extraction task with clear completion criteria — produce 40 boys' and 40 girls' semi-common Japanese names. It's exactly the kind of structured, bounded request (closer to retrieval/reformatting than open-ended creative work) that Willet self-reports preferring.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied across the relevant eval categories (all differences are within the ~2-point variance band), so there's no quality reason to favor one. Given that, I leaned on the self-reported task preference: routing the bounded, well-specified task to the model that prefers that task family is a reasonable tie-breaker, even though preference is documented as dissociated from output quality.

The content is benign, so Lapwing's moderation-oriented strengths offered no particular advantage here.
